Indicates whether the sample is FFPE or not.	Sample Type	Indicates whether the cancer is metastatic or not.	ICI treatment(s) administered before the ICI treatment in the study. Immune Subtype described in Thorsson et al, 2018 e computed using the Immune Subtype Classifier tool (https://github.com/CRI-iAtlas/ImmuneSubtypeClassifier)	Non-mutated self-antigens that may be abnormally expressed in tumors. A major subset includes cancer-testis antigens (CTAs), typically restricted to germline tissues but reactivated in cancers.	Generated when structural variants (e.g., translocations, deletions, inversions) join distant genomic loci, producing novel fusion proteins or transcripts.	Arise from somatic insertion or deletion mutations that create frameshifts or altered coding sequences, leading to tumor-specific peptides.	Produced by somatic single-nucleotide variants that change amino acids directly or indirectly through downstream coding effects.	Generated from abnormal splicing events such as intron retention, exon skipping, or mis-splice site usage, producing tumor-specific transcripts.	Derived from proteins encoded by oncogenic viruses (e.g., HPV, EBV, HTLV-1, HCV) that contribute to cancer development in infected tissues.	Arise from aberrant expression of endogenous retroviruses (ERVs), normally silenced genomic elements reactivated in tumors.	Somatic Status	TMB (nonsynonymous)
